'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**An [[ambush]] on a convoy by suspected [[Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army|MNDAA]] [[insurgent]]s in [[Shan State]], [[Myanmar]], kills nine civilians and three policemen, and injures 13 others. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/myanmar-12-killed-in-armed-attack20210206101849/ (ANI News)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[United Nations]] says that the [[Government of Ethiopia|Ethiopian government]] is blocking [[humanitarian aid|aid]] from going to 2.3 million people in non-government-controlled rural areas in [[Tigray Region|Tigray]] who are in dire need of assistance. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/ethiopian-government-blocking-aid-tigray-un-says (''VOA'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**A bombing targeting a [[Hinduism|Hindu]] shop in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], kills three people. Attacks against Hindu and [[Sikhism|Sikh]] minorities increased in the country in the last years, mainly by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|Islamic State]] militants. [https://gandhara.rferl.org/a/blast-in-kabul-wounds-members-of-the-minority-hindu-community/31089101.html (Gandhara)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Cuba]]
**The [[Cuba]]n [[Council of Ministers (Cuba)|Council of Ministers]] approves a measure authorizing [[Private sector|private activity]] in most sectors. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/cuba-authorizes-private-activity-in-majority-of-sectors-1.5299104 (AFP via CTV News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eleven people are dead and three others have been rescued after their wooden boat overturns in a lake in [[Susong County]], in east [[China]]'s [[Anhui]] [[provinces of China|province]]. [https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2021-02-06/doc-ikftssap4429310.shtml (Sina)]
*Four skiers are killed and four others are injured in an avalanche in [[Millcreek Canyon (Salt Lake County, Utah)|Millcreek Canyon]], [[Utah]], [[United States]]. [https://www.fox13now.com/news/local-news/four-skiers-killed-in-millcreek-canyon-avalanche (KSTU-TV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri]]
*****[[Missouri]] reports its first case of [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in an adult from [[Marion County, Missouri|Marion County]]. [https://www.kmov.com/news/missouri-reports-first-case-of-uk-covid-19-variant/article_544044ce-68f3-11eb-a019-0783dc43cc4a.amp.html (KMOV-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[Canada]] surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.cp24.com/news/canada-hits-800-000-total-cases-of-covid-19-top-doctor-says-numbers-trending-down-1.5298920 (CP24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]]'s [[National Medical Products Administration]] gives a conditional approval to [[Sinovac]]'s [[Coronavac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for general use. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210206-covid-19-china-approves-sinovac-vaccine-for-general-public-use (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 61 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,989. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-02/06/c_139726077.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Myanmar]] approves the use of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine developed by [[Russia]]. [https://sputnikvaccine.com/newsroom/pressreleases/sputnik-v-authorized-in-myanmar/ (Sputnik V)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The [[Government of South Korea|government]] eases the restrictions on business operating hours outside of the [[Seoul Capital Area]], allowing those businesses to operate until 10 p.m. local time amid a backlash over prolonged restrictions. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20210206000024 (''The Korea Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] signs a decree authorizing the emergency use of [[monoclonal antibody|monoclonal antibodies]] to treat [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] patients. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-italy/italy-clears-emergency-use-of-covid-19-antibody-therapies-idUSS8N2AH04Y (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19. [https://nltimes.nl/2021/02/06/infections-hospitalizations-continue-fall-netherlands-surpasses-1-million-positive-cases (''NL Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Immigration policy of the Joe Biden administration]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] suspends and initiates the process to terminate the [[Donald Trump|Trump]]-era "Asylum Cooperative" agreements with [[El Salvador]], [[Guatemala]] and [[Honduras]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-centralamerica/biden-administration-suspends-trump-asylum-deals-with-el-salvador-guatemala-honduras-idUSKBN2A702Q (Reuters)]
*The leaders of [[Palau]], the [[Federated States of Micronesia]], [[Nauru]], [[Kiribati]], and the [[Marshall Islands]] will meet on Monday to discuss leaving the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] after Marshallese candidate [[Gerald Zackios]] was not chosen as Secretary-General. Palau had earlier announced that it was leaving the forum. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/435911/micronesian-leaders-to-debate-leaving-pacific-islands-forum (RNZ)]
*[[Moussa Faki]] is re-elected as [[Chairperson of the African Union Commission|Chairperson]] of the [[African Union Commission]]. [http://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/2/10/402476/World/Africa/AU-leader-Faki-reelected-for-second-year-term-Offi.aspx (AFP via ''Al-Ahram'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
***Governor [[Gavin Newsom]] issues revised COVID-19 mitigation guidelines for churches after the [[United States Supreme Court|U.S. Supreme Court]] lifts the state's ban on indoor worship in areas hardest hit by the pandemic. The new guidelines limit indoor services to 25 percent of the church's capacity in hard-hit areas and restricts indoor singing and chanting. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/california-revise-indoor-church-guidelines-ruling-75730702 (ABC News)]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**An Australian economic advisor to [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] reveals that he has been detained by the [[Tatmadaw]]. He is the first foreign national confirmed to be in the custody of Myanmar's military. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/02/06/australian-economic-advisor-to-suu-kyi-says-detained-in-myanmar-bbc (AFP via ''The Star'')]
*After a juggler is shot dead by a [[Carabineros de Chile|Carabinero]], several protests are held in [[Panguipulli]], southern [[Chile]]. The protests escalate into [[riot]]s and several buildings, including the city hall, [[arson|are burned]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/06/world/americas/chile-police-shooting.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Egypt]] frees [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] journalist [[Mahmoud Hussein]] after four years in detention. He had been held on charges of spreading false news, joining a banned group and receiving foreign funds. [https://www.voanews.com/press-freedom/egypt-frees-al-jazeera-journalist-after-4-years-detention (VOA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*French religious sister [[Nathalie Becquart]] is named by [[Pope Francis]] one of the Undersecretaries of the [[Synod of Bishops in the Catholic Church|Synod of Bishops]], becoming the first woman to reach that office and having a right to vote in the Synod. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/07/europe/pope-synod-appointment-intl-scli/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship in Myanmar]], aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**The [[State Administrative Council|military junta]] shuts down the country's [[internet in Myanmar|internet]] with a near-total blackout in effect amid growing protests against the coup. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-55960284 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[10th Annual NFL Honors]]
**In [[American football]], [[Green Bay Packers]] [[quarterback]] [[Aaron Rodgers]] wins his third [[National Football League Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] award, making him the sixth player to do so after [[Jim Brown]], [[Brett Favre]], [[Johnny Unitas]], [[Peyton Manning]], and [[Tom Brady]]. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/sports-pmn/nfl-awards-aaron-rodgers-earns-3rd-mvp (''National Post'')] [https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2926052-packers-aaron-rodgers-wins-2020-nfl-mvp-award (Bleacher Report)]
